specAnchors.text: know that: • the universe is a large collection of billions of galaxies • a galaxy is a large collection of billions of stars • our solar system is in the Milky Way galaxy

primer.text: Cosmology has a ladder of scale: billions of galaxies make up the universe, billions of stars make up each galaxy, and one ordinary star — the Sun — anchors our own solar system inside the Milky Way. Keep the three levels straight and every 'place it in the hierarchy' question becomes easy marks.

modules.title: The universe and galaxies
modules.opening: The universe is the entirety of space and everything in it — a vast collection of billions of galaxies. Each galaxy, in turn, gathers billions of stars into one vast assembly — enormous glowing objects like the Sun populate it.
keyPoints: Billions of galaxies, gathered together, make up the universe — the largest scale of all.
The universe is also the name for the entirety of space.
Galaxies gather billions of stars into one vast assembly.
Stars are huge glowing spheres of gas, like the Sun.

low.restatement: Universe = billions of galaxies; galaxy = billions of stars.
low.analogy: Cities and countries: stars are houses, galaxies are cities, the universe is the whole planet of cities.
low.examPointer: Definition questions want the 'billions' wording on both levels — quote it.

medium.restatement: Two nested collections define the ladder: stars within galaxies, galaxies within the universe, which also names all of space.
medium.analogy: A Russian doll set: each layer holds many of the layer below, and the outermost doll is the universe.
medium.examPointer: Smallest-to-largest ordering questions are near-guaranteed marks: star, galaxy, universe.

modules.title: Our solar system
modules.opening: Our solar system sits inside the Milky Way galaxy. The Sun — a star — sits at its centre, and Earth ranks third among the eight planets orbiting it.
keyPoints: Our Solar System is part of the Milky Way galaxy.
The Sun, a star, sits at the centre of our Solar System.
Earth ranks third among the Solar System's eight planets.
In a planetary system, planets and other objects orbit a central star.

low.restatement: Sun at the centre, Earth third of eight planets, all inside the Milky Way.
low.analogy: A house (Earth) on one street (Solar System) in one city (Milky Way) on a whole continent of cities (universe).
low.examPointer: 'Third of eight planets' is the exact phrase examiners look for.

medium.restatement: Containment runs planet → planetary system → galaxy → universe, with the Sun as the system's central star.
medium.analogy: A passenger (Earth) in a car (Solar System) in a car park (galaxy) in a city of car parks (universe).
medium.examPointer: Hierarchy questions fail when students put the galaxy inside the solar system — drill the containment direction.

glossary.definition: The entirety of space: billions of galaxies gathered into one whole.
A large collection of billions of stars, such as the Milky Way.
The planets and other objects orbiting our central star, the Sun.

figures.alt: Diagram illustrating the universe, Milky Way Galaxy, and our solar system with labelled planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
figures.caption: The universe holds galaxies; the Milky Way holds our Solar System around the Sun
